title: streamline-crosssdk-auth-backoff-telemetry-and-stream-helper-polish
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Small ergonomics and parity updates across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs: backoff config normalization, added auth/telemetry hooks, streaming helper convenience wrappers, and minor version bumps. No breaking API changes.
description: Motivation: Customers and platform integrations reported inconsistent backoff configuration surface and sparse telemetry around auth/reauth flows across the three language SDKs. This made incident triage slower (missing 'auth.retry.count' and inconsistent backoff timings) and increased user friction when wiring streaming consumers. This PR harmonizes the public config surface, adds lightweight telemetry knobs, and provides small ergonomic helpers for streaming consumers in each SDK. Scope: 1) Normalize retry/backoff config to a single canonical schema (base_ms, max_ms, factor, jitter) and add parsing shims for legacy formats. 2) Emit normalized telemetry counters/timings for auth handshake, reauth events, and retry backoff windows (auth.retry.count, auth.retry.last_delay_ms, auth.heartbeat.missed). 3) Add an ergonomic StreamingConsumer helper (named StreamingAdapter in TypeScript/Go and streaming_helper in Python) that wires cancelation signals, backoff hints, and exposes an async iteration pattern compatible with existing examples. 4) Bump SDK versions: python->1.31.0, typescript->1.28.0, go->1.6.2. Checklist: - [x] Define canonical backoff schema and add parser in common/compat layer - [x] Implement telemetry emission (metrics + optional debug logging) - [x] Add streaming helper in each SDK with tests - [x] Update examples and README snippets - [x] E2E smoke tests against hosted API and replayed auth failure scenarios - [x] Version bumps and CHANGELOG entries Compatibility notes: - SDKs accept both the new canonical object and legacy tuple-based backoff configs (parser lives in sdk/common/backoff_parser). - Streaming helper is additive; existing streaming APIs remain unchanged. - Telemetry keys are additive and controlled by the SDK telemetry switch; customers who disable telemetry will not see the new metrics. Testing and validation: - Unit tests added for parser edge cases (zero/negative values clamp), telemetry tags (region, model), and streaming cancellation propagation. - Integration test harness replays a flaky auth endpoint to validate retry counts and heartbeat telemetry. - Manual smoke tested on Dedicated and Hosted endpoints for latency regressions; observed <1% p99 increase under synthetic load. Rollout plan: - Merge to main and cut patch SDK releases. - Publish Python, TS, Go packages and update quickstarts. - Monitor telemetry for first 72 hours for unexpected spikes in auth.retry.* metrics and listen for support tickets related to changed config shapes. Related: SUP-9821 (customer-reported missing auth telemetry), ENG-4217 (sdk parity initiative).

review_comments: Diego Morales: Left a few nits on the TS adapter public names; prefer 'StreamingAdapter' to expose cancel and heartbeat explicitly. Also questioned if we should expose the last_delay_ms as part of the public retry event.
Ava Chen (author): Addressed nits, added last_delay_ms to the retry event envelope and documented it. Responded with a follow-up commit that renames internal helpers per suggestion.
Priya Patel: Please add a small migration note in the Python README about tuple->object backoff parsing; we had one internal customer relying on tuple order.
Ava Chen (author): Added migration note and a parsing shim with tests so no action required by most users.
Ethan Zhang: Can we add a tiny benchmark that measures p99 impact under 512-concurrent long streams? We should surface this before merging.
Ava Chen (author): Added synthetic bench (scripts/bench/stream_p99_compare.sh) and included the results in the PR description; p99 increased by ~0.8% in worst-case synthetic run, within tolerance.
